q: Does CBAM apply to brassware exported from Moradabad?
title: Moradabad brassware and CBAM
short: No. Brass is a copper alloy, and copper articles in Chapter 74 are not CBAM goods. Steel or aluminium items in a Moradabad shipment may be, if declared under a covered heading. Buyers of brassware may still ask for a footprint per kg built from melting fuel, electricity and metal bought.
audience: Brassware, metal handicraft and hardware exporters in the Moradabad cluster of Uttar Pradesh

p: Chapter 74 copper and copper alloy articles, including brass artware, are outside Annex I.

ul: 7326 other articles of iron or steel: covered.

p: Melting fuel and electricity give the making-stage figure; brass ingots and scrap bought in carry most of the footprint and sit in Scope 3.

senseible: Senseible reads the energy invoices behind the making stage into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, and keeps material invoices on the Scope 3 trail. Material factors come from your supplier or a named database and are labelled with their source, so the product figure can be traced line by line.
